meta.project: Integrated ESG-ABSA Framework for Multilingual and Explainable Reasoning
meta.description: Systematic reference mapping between integrated research objectives (v-1 to v3) and curated NLP/LLM literature evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Improving Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer between Closely Related Languages by injecting Character-level Noise
literature_references.relevance: Supports C3 and RQ1.1 by demonstrating that character-level noise improves zero-shot transfer for closely related languages, providing a method for regional calibration of Indonesian and English dialects.

literature_references.title: Morphosyntactic Tagging with Pre-trained Language Models for Arabic and its Dialects
literature_references.authors: Go Inoue, Salam Khalifa, Nizar Habash
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical evidence that strategic fine-tuning with high-resource data benefits low-resource dialects, justifying the approach for C1 (bilingual Indonesian engine).

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?

literature_references.title: Cutting Down on Prompts and Parameters: Simple Few-Shot Learning with Language Models
literature_references.authors: Robert L. Logan, Ivana Balazevic, Eric Wallace, Fabio Petroni, Sameer Singh, Sebastian Riedel
literature_references.relevance: Validates the few-shot strategies in RQ2.1 and C16, showing that updating only 0.1% of parameters can outperform standard fine-tuning in low-resource settings.

literature_references.title: Learning to Robustly Aggregate Labeling Functions for Semi-supervised Data Programming
literature_references.authors: Ayush Maheshwari, KrishnaTeja Killamsetty, Ganesh Ramakrishnan, Rishabh Iyer, Marina Danilevsky, Lucian Popa
literature_references.relevance: Provides the algorithmic foundation for C16 by proposing reweighting frameworks for noisy labeling functions in semi-supervised paradigms.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?

literature_references.title: Fact-Tree Reasoning for N-ary Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
literature_references.authors: Yao Zhang, Peiyao Li, Hongru Liang, Adam Jatowt, Zhenglu Yang
literature_references.relevance: Causal evidence for C7 and RQ3.2, illustrating how iterative fact-tree reasoning improves accuracy and interpretability compared to chain-based methods.

literature_references.title: BiSyn-GAT+: Bi-Syntax Aware Graph Attention Network for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
literature_references.authors: Shuo Liang, Wei Wei, Xian-Ling Mao, Fei Wang, Zhiyong He
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C15 by demonstrating that exploiting hierarchical syntax/trees reduces noise in aspect-sentiment alignment, critical for ontology-grounded ABSA.

research_questions: RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?
RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?

literature_references.title: Table-based Fact Verification with Self-adaptive Mixture of Experts
literature_references.authors: Yuxuan Zhou, Xien Liu, Kaiyin Zhou, Ji Wu
literature_references.relevance: Supports C11 and RQ4.5 by providing a mixture-of-experts model to handle numerical and logical reasoning over tabular data (KPIs) to verify narrative claims.

literature_references.title: BBQ: A hand-built bias benchmark for question answering
literature_references.authors: Alicia Parrish, Angelica Chen, Nikita Nangia, Vishakh Padmakumar, Jason Phang, Jana Thompson, Phu Mon Htut, Sam Bowman
literature_references.relevance: Establishes a baseline for identifying social and narrative biases (RQ4.1) by testing whether model choices override correct choice in biased contexts.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: ED2LM: Encoder-Decoder to Language Model for Faster Document Re-ranking Inference
literature_references.authors: Kai Hui, Honglei Zhuang, Tao Chen, Zhen Qin, Jing Lu, Dara Bahri, Ji Ma, Jai Gupta, C. D. Santos, Yi Tay, Donald Metzler
literature_references.relevance: Enables the scalability goals of C12 and RQ5.2 by showing how encoder-decoder architectures can be decomposed for faster inference speeds up to 6.8X.

literature_references.title: Using Interactive Feedback to Improve the Accuracy and Explainability of Question Answering Systems Post-Deployment
literature_references.authors: Zichao Li, Yiran Wang, M. Utiyama, E. Sumita, Hai Zhao, Taro Watanabe
literature_references.relevance: Supports C12's dashboard goal by proving that interactive correction loops post-deployment enhance stakeholder trust and overall parse accuracy.
